summary.text: 后 is attested for a ruler and a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes the separate word “after/behind,” represented by 後 in traditional Chinese; this spelling loan is attributed to sound similarity, though its ancient sound basis is unresolved.

formation.text: The graph’s early formation is disputed. An early lexicographic account describes a human issuing commands and analyzes the graph with 一 and 口. Other accounts connect early forms with 司 or 毓, but none establishes a secure decomposition of the received graph.

components.text: 口 appears in an early lexicographic analysis of a human issuing commands. This identifies it as a component in that account, but does not establish its independent role in the graph’s origin.

history.text: Accounts of the early graph differ: one treats 后 and 司 as the same graph, with orientation distinguishing them in bronze forms; another reports an oracle form written with 毓. Neither establishes a sequence leading to the received form.
The received form contains 口, but the early lexicographic analysis does not explain how this visible form arose.
后 was used in some texts to write the separate word represented by 後. It later became the standardized simplified form of 後.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s early origin remains disputed. Childbirth and rear-body interpretations have been proposed, but neither a depiction nor a secure component analysis is established by the cited accounts.
The earliest date for using 后 to write the separate word 後 remains unresolved; the cited accounts document the spelling loan and later standardization but do not establish when the loan began.

senses.period: Late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions; primary examples not independently verified
senses.text: A late Spring and Autumn bronze use is reported with the meaning “ruler.” Any earlier oracle use of the same graph and word is not securely dated here.

senses.period: Received textual usage; transition date unresolved
senses.text: Received-text examples document 后 for a ruler’s principal wife. They do not establish when, or whether, this sense developed from “ruler.”

senses.period: Classical spelling use reported; precise chronology unresolved; current in simplified Chinese
senses.text: In simplified Chinese, 后 writes the separate word “after/behind,” represented by 後 in traditional Chinese. This is a spelling loan, not a documented change in 后’s meaning. An ancient sound match is reported but not established here.

developments.text: Both senses are documented, but their relationship and any development between them are unresolved.

The graph 后 was reused to write the distinct word represented by 後 because the words were reported to sound alike or similarly. The ancient sound basis and the loan’s precise chronology are unresolved.

limitations.text: The available attestations do not establish a dated semantic chain from childbirth or succession to “ruler” or “empress.”

overview.text: 后 is attested for a ruler and a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes “after/behind”: the separate graph 後 was borrowed because the words were reported to sound alike, though an ancient sound match is unconfirmed.

components.text: An early account includes 口 in its picture of a command-giving ruler, but does not establish 口’s independent role in the graph’s origin.
